author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Either form of the veterinarian directory can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty. Matching is on the whole name and ignores letter case. A blank name asks for the whole directory, an unheld name answers a normal empty directory, and paging keeps the narrowing.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is opened for it, then only those veterinarians are listed, a page at a time
given that same specialty, when the machine-readable directory is requested for it, then only those veterinarians are returned
given a name differing from a held specialty only by letter case, when either form is asked for it, then it matches
given only part of a held specialty's name, when either form is asked for it, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is asked for it, then a normal directory is answered with nobody in it, not a refusal
given a blank or space-only specialty, when either form is asked for it, then every veterinarian is listed, as if none had been named
given spaces around a named specialty, when either form is asked for it, then the result matches the same name without them (edge case 2)
given a narrowed directory running to more than one page, when a page link is followed, then that page stays narrowed to the same specialty
given the same named specialty, when both forms are asked for it, then they answer with the same veterinarians (edge case 3)
given no specialty named at all, when either form is opened, then it behaves exactly as before this slice, including REQ-VET-003's full machine-readable list
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for picking a specialty on either surface
free-text or by-name search over veterinarians, and any search over pets or visits (NG-9 as narrowed)
narrowing to more than one specialty at once
managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2)
notes: Autofix audit: the log carried no prd-autofix records at dispatch, so none were audited. REQ-VET-003 is minted alongside REQ-VET-004 and records the machine-readable directory as a supported surface; it needs no new behavior, only the regression criterion listed above. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. Two follow-ups sit outside this agent's write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-30-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md, and docs/system-design.md maps the two vet routes to REQ-VET-001 only. Four open questions recorded in the PRD: a visible control, multiple specialties at once, who consumes the machine-readable form, and whether spaces around a name are ignored (edge case 2 takes the owner-search reading).

scope_overrides.owner_decision: **Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed.** Free-text veterinarian *search* stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is now in scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter extends the existing vet feature package with no new package, type, or layer. It follows the owner-search precedent for shape (derived repository query plus paged controller, no service layer, per ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization) and departs from it on two points recorded in a new ADR: matching is made case-insensitive inside the query rather than by column collation, and the filtered reads carry no @Cacheable. docs/system-design.md now maps both vet routes to REQ-VET-001, REQ-VET-003, and REQ-VET-004, states the vet directory's read invariants under Contracts, and carries a Threat Model row for the caller-supplied cache key.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived reads for one specialty name: a paged one for the HTML route and a collection one for the serialized route. Suggested signatures: Page<Vet> findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String specialty, Pageable pageable) and Collection<Vet> findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String specialty). The underscore makes the specialties.name traversal explicit. Keep @Transactional(readOnly = true); add no @Cacheable (see risks).

VetController: both handlers take @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty. One private normalizer strips the value and maps null-or-blank to null, and both handlers call it. This single normalization is what makes edge case 2 (surrounding spaces) and edge case 3 (both forms answer alike) hold by construction rather than by two parallel code paths.

VetController dispatch: a null normalized value calls the existing findAll paths unchanged, which preserves REQ-VET-001 and REQ-VET-003 exactly; a non-null value calls the new methods. The owner trick of an empty string standing for the broadest search does not carry over, because equality matching has no such identity value.
addPaginationModel adds the normalized specialty to the model so vetList.html can put it back on the paging links.

vetList.html: replace the eight @{'/vets.html?page=__${...}__'} preprocessing concatenations with the parameterized link form @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}. The link expression URL-encodes the caller-supplied value; string concatenation does not.

patterns.description: derived paged query taking a search term plus Pageable — the shape the two new VetRepository methods follow
request-parameter normalization in the controller (null check then strip) — the precedent for the vet normalizer, minus the empty-string-means-all trick
shouldFindVets: @DataJpaTest against seeded H2 data. Vet 3 (Douglas) holds dentistry and surgery, so it anchors the ignore-case and partial-name repository tests

risks.risk: VetControllerTests substitutes VetRepository with @MockitoBean, so a case-insensitivity test written there proves only that the controller passes the string through. The generated SQL is never exercised, and theSpecialtyFilterShouldIgnoreLetterCase would pass against a case-sensitive query.
risks.mitigation: Prove matching semantics (ignore-case, whole-name-only, empty result) in ClinicServiceTests against real H2 data; keep the controller tests for parameter binding, surface parity, blank handling, and link rendering.

risks.risk: Caching the filtered read would key the eviction-free, size-unlimited vets cache on a caller-supplied string, so any client could grow it without bound.
risks.mitigation: The new repository methods carry no @Cacheable. Recorded in the new ADR and as a Threat Model row in docs/system-design.md.

risks.risk: Relying on column collation for case-insensitivity is what makes owner search case-sensitive under PostgreSQL (Known Defects). The specialties.name column has no ignore-case typing in any vendor schema.
risks.mitigation: Use the IgnoreCase keyword so the comparison is generated into the query and holds on all three vendors.

risks.risk: A derived query over the EAGER @ManyToMany specialties association can multiply rows and corrupt page counts if a vet joins more than one matching row.
risks.mitigation: Equality on one name yields at most one join row per vet given distinct specialty names; the seeded names are distinct and the application has no write path for specialties (NG-2). Use a derived query rather than an explicit join fetch, so pagination stays in SQL. If specialties ever gain a write path, Distinct becomes necessary.

risks.risk: A null specialty model attribute may render as a bare specialty= in the paging links on the unfiltered page, changing today's markup.
risks.mitigation: Harmless by construction: a blank specialty is defined to behave as absent (acceptance criterion 6), so such a link returns the unfiltered page. Verify the rendered form during the Red/Green loop and assert whichever holds; do not reintroduce string concatenation to avoid it.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so none was audited. Doc writes in this dispatch: new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-30-vet-specialty-filter-query.md; index rows in docs/adr/README.md for that ADR and for the 2026-08-30 non-goal ADR (the PRD expert's flagged follow-up); Implements column, vet-directory invariant paragraph, Threat Model row, and Open Question 5 updated in docs/system-design.md. Stale-state correction: docs/system-design.md listed 'The machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' under Known Defects; REQ-VET-003 records that route as a supported surface, so the row was removed, and the withdrawal trail stays in the PRD's Superseded section. Negative precedent, outside this slice: owners/ownersList.html builds its paging links without the lastName search term, so owner search paging drops the filter — do not copy that link shape into vetList.html, and whether owner search has the same defect is a question for the PRD owner. No new dependency, no new package, no change to the module dependency graph. Trust boundary: the specialty parameter is bound as a query parameter, reaches the database only through a parameter-bound derived query, and reaches HTML only through a Thymeleaf link expression.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: both new repository methods are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase). The property path is fixed in the method name at compile time; the caller value binds as a JPA query parameter. No string-concatenated JPQL/SQL, no caller-controlled Sort property (VetController builds PageRequest.of(page-1, 5) with no sort argument), no dynamic property expression. Repository-wide grep confirms no concatenated query survives in the vet package.

Cache: no @Cacheable leaked onto either filtered read. Grep over the vet package finds exactly two @Cacheable("vets") sites, both on the pre-existing unfiltered findAll overloads; the remaining hits are Javadoc prose. No class-level @Cacheable or @CacheConfig on VetRepository or VetController, so the caller-supplied specialty never becomes a cache key. The ADR's reasoning holds as written in code, and docs/system-design.md Threat Model carries the matching row.

XSS: no concatenation of the caller value survives in vetList.html. All five paging links use parameterized link expressions @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}; the two remaining __${...}__ preprocessing sites were removed. Thymeleaf URL-encodes link parameters and HTML-escapes the th:href attribute value; the controller test asserts a&b surgery renders as specialty=a%26b%20surgery. The specialty attribute reaches the template only through those link expressions -- no th:text, th:utext, th:inline, or inline-JS reflection of it anywhere in templates/. Reflected XSS is not reachable on this path.

JSON endpoint: /vets serializes only the Vets wrapper over Vet entities (id, first/last name, specialties). The specialty request parameter is not echoed into the response, and the filtered result is a strict subset of what the pre-existing unfiltered route already returns publicly, so the filter opens no new data exposure. Nothing in the response is caller-influenced beyond which rows are selected.

Input handling: normalizeSpecialty strips and null-collapses in one place shared by both routes, so the two routes cannot diverge in what they treat as a filter. No length, charset, or pattern constraint is needed -- the value only reaches a bound query parameter and a URL-encoded link.
Secrets: swept the diff for token/password/secret/key/credential and datasource-shaped strings. No hardcoded credential is introduced; the only literals added are specialty names and test fixtures.

Supply chain: build.gradle, gradle.properties, and gradle/ are unchanged in the change set -- no dependency added, removed, or version-shifted, so this change introduces no new CVE surface. No dependencyCheck plugin is configured in build.gradle.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The two null-specialty branch points use two different shapes for the same 'null means unfiltered' decision: findPaginated uses an if/early-return, showResourcesVetList uses a ternary inline in the addAll(...) call. A reader who compares the two handlers (they're meant to answer the same request alike, per the shared normalizer's own javadoc) sees two idioms for one decision and has to check both read the same before trusting that.
findings.fix: Pick one shape for both call sites -- e.g. give showResourcesVetList the same if/early-return-style local (Collection<Vet> vets = specialty == null ? ... : ...; on its own line) so both handlers express the null-check identically, or extract a tiny private helper the two callers share.

approved_aspects: VetRepository's two new derived methods are correctly documented, including a why-comment for the deliberate absence of @Cacheable that cross-references the ADR
normalizeSpecialty is a single, well-named, well-documented seam shared by both routes, exactly matching the design-block's guidance and eliminating duplicate null/blank handling
vetList.html's parameterized link expressions (@{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}) correctly replace the old string-concatenation links and get URL-encoding for free
No naming, package, or layering violations; checkFormat and checkstyleMain pass clean; no prohibited suffixes, no swallowed exceptions, no new mutable state

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The four new repository tests (shouldFindVetsBySpecialtyIgnoringCase, shouldNotFindVetsByPartialSpecialtyName, shouldFindNoVetsForSpecialtyNobodyHolds, shouldFindVetsBySpecialtyInPages) were added on 2026-08-30, after testing-principles.md's Test Naming cutover, but keep the pre-existing should{Verb} style instead of the mandated the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school. The Factory Methods section carries an explicit 'no sweep of the existing suite required' exemption for old tests, but the Test Naming section applies to 'tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward' with no such exemption for a file whose surrounding tests predate it — these four are new tests squarely in scope for the school.
findings.fix: Rename to something like theSpecialtyFilterShouldIgnoreLetterCase, theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchAPartialSpecialtyName, theSpecialtyFilterShouldAnswerAnEmptyDirectoryWhenNoVetHoldsIt, theSpecialtyFilterShouldPageMatchingVets — recovering the PRD's own test_names for the first three, which the build-pass notes only as a placement change, not a naming one.

findings.description: No controller-level test exercises a specialty no vet holds. Acceptance criterion 5 ('a normal directory is answered with nobody in it, not a refusal') is a claim about the HTTP surface (status 200, not 404/error) that the repository-level shouldFindNoVetsForSpecialtyNobodyHolds cannot prove — that test only shows the derived query returns an empty Collection, never that VetController.showVetList/showResourcesVetList propagate an empty result as a normal 200 response rather than special-casing it. The design-block's stated rationale for moving PRD tests to ClinicServiceTests was specifically the case-sensitivity risk of a mocked repository; that rationale does not extend to this criterion, since the mock trivially returns an empty list here and the thing under test is the controller's handling of it, not the query's matching semantics.
findings.fix: Add a controller test (e.g. theSpecialtyFilterShouldAnswerAnEmptyDirectoryWhenNoVetHoldsIt) stubbing vets.findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(...) to return an empty Collection/PageImpl for both /vets.html and /vets (JSON) and asserting status().isOk() with an empty listVets / $.vetList.length() == 0.

approved_aspects: Test placement judgment call is correct: moving the case-insensitivity, partial-name, and no-match matching-semantics assertions into ClinicServiceTests against real H2 is the only way to prove the generated SQL, since VetControllerTests substitutes VetRepository with @MockitoBean and would pass a case-insensitivity assertion against a case-sensitive query — the design-block's stated risk is real and the mitigation is sound.
All ten PRD acceptance criteria have coverage somewhere in the two files except the empty-directory-is-a-normal-200 half of criterion 5 at the controller layer (see finding).

theUnfilteredPaginationLinksShouldPageTheWholeDirectory correctly proves both the bare specialty= link rendering and that following it returns the unfiltered directory, resolving the open question the design-block flagged about that markup.

Mocking stays within policy: MockitoBean on VetRepository is the same tolerated pre-existing pattern (not new), and MockMvc is the sanctioned HTTP-boundary substitute; no internal collaborator is newly mocked.
AssertJ used fluently in ClinicServiceTests (extracting/containsExactly/isEmpty); full build (./gradlew test) passes, 0 failures.
Four-phase structure and derived-from-input assertions are respected in the new tests; no phase-comment narration was introduced.

approved_aspects: BDD naming fix verified: the four ClinicServiceTests methods (theSpecialtyFilterShouldIgnoreLetterCase, theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchAPartialSpecialtyName, theSpecialtyFilterShouldAnswerAnEmptyDirectoryWhenNoVetHoldsIt, theSpecialtyFilterShouldPageMatchingVets) now follow the mandated the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school and recover the PRD's own wording for the first three, matching the suggested fix exactly.

Controller-level empty-result coverage added: theSpecialtyNoVetHoldsShouldBeAnsweredWithAnEmptyDirectoryNotAnError stubs both the Collection and Page overloads of findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase for cardiology and asserts status().isOk() with an empty listVets on /vets.html and $.vetList.length()==0 on /vets -- this is the HTTP-surface proof of acceptance criterion 5 that the repository-level test could not provide, since the controller mocks the repository.

The name-collision resolution is sound: the implementer kept the PRD-aligned name on the repository test (which proves the query's matching semantics) and gave the controller test a distinct name (theSpecialtyNoVetHoldsShouldBeAnsweredWithAnEmptyDirectoryNotAnError) that still conforms to the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school. The two tests prove different things at different layers -- one that the derived query returns no rows for an unheld specialty, the other that the controller propagates an empty result as a normal 200 rather than special-casing it -- so distinct names are the correct call, not a naming-policy violation. Swept both test files for further duplicate method names across the two classes: none found.

Code-quality fix (extracted private findAll(String) so both VetController handlers share the same if/early-return null-check shape) does not alter test-observable behavior; full ./gradlew test run (34s) passes with 0 failures, including both fixed test classes.
No new mocking-policy, four-phase-structure, or AssertJ-style issues introduced by the delta; the new controller test matches the established pattern of its sibling tests in the same file.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Ten files, but the production reach is three: two derived reads on VetRepository, one normalizer plus two handler signatures in VetController, and the paging links in vetList.html. No sensitive paths, no schema change, no new package or layer, and both new URL parameters are optional, so the existing HTML and JSON contracts stay backward compatible. The remaining files are tests and docs.

semantic_surprise.note: I probed the four places this shape usually hides a surprise and each one holds. Case-insensitive matching is expressed by the IgnoreCase keyword rather than by column collation, so it does not repeat the PostgreSQL divergence recorded for owner search, and a real-H2 test proves it. Paging over the specialties join returns a correct total of two with page size one, not a join-inflated count. Blank and space-only names collapse to null through one normalizer both routes share, so the two forms cannot diverge. The template rewrite from string-interpolated paging links to Thymeleaf link expressions is wider than the requirement strictly needed, but it is the correct construction, it URL-encodes the name, and it is asserted both for an ampersand-bearing name and for the unfiltered page, whose links now carry a bare empty specialty parameter that round-trips to the whole directory. One latent naming hazard is worth knowing rather than fixing: vetList.html already binds specialty as a th:each loop variable inside the table row, and the new model attribute shares that name. The paging block sits outside the loop, so nothing is shadowed today.

test_adequacy.note: The tests split along the line that matters and assert real outcomes rather than restating the code. Query semantics (letter case, whole-name matching, empty match, real paging) run against H2 in ClinicServiceTests, where a case-sensitive query would actually fail. HTTP surface behavior (binding, blank-as-absent, an empty result answered 200 rather than an error, link carry-through, percent-encoding) runs through MockMvc against rendered content and JSON. That placement is deliberate: the controller tests substitute the repository, so a case-insensitivity assertion there would have passed against a case-sensitive query. Both gaps the test-reviewer named were closed rather than argued away.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved, and the two that opened with changes_requested closed with empty findings lists and verification prose naming the specific fixes. The two bar_clause findings were satisfied by changing the code to meet the bar, not by relaxing the clause. No escalate tag and no lingering caveat inside an approval. The security review independently confirmed the injection, cache-key, XSS, and exposure edges I checked.

scope_deviation.note: The code lands exactly on the surface the product owner fixed: a URL contract on both routes, one named specialty, no visible control, no multi-specialty filtering. The single design revision was bookkeeping rather than rework -- the build stopped on an autofix audit whose path coverage omitted two doc files, and the superseding design-block carried the guidance forward unchanged with no implementation change. The four questions the slice could not settle were left open in the PRD rather than answered by fiat.

rationale: Every edge where this shape usually hides a defect is proven against a real database or recorded as a decision: matching, paging, blank names, link encoding. Confirm the two product calls -- filtered reads bypass the vets cache by design, so each one reaches the database, and REQ-VET-003 promotes a route the PRD had listed as pending removal -- then merge.
